submitted.rationale: Index 4 (Co0.785Sb0.215) had the only positive EQE of the three measurements (0.0022%). It lies in the Co-rich spinel region, near Co7Sb2O12, which MACE puts close to the hull; MEGNet gives it a 1.44 eV gap, low enough to absorb 2.4 eV light. All three values are close to zero, so this whole composition line looks like a weak photoanode system.

rejected.reason: Trirutile CoSb2O6 is on the MACE hull, but the measured EQE was about zero (-0.0029%).
GP-UCB pick in the mid-range; measured EQE was -0.0014%. MACE puts CoSbO4 0.12 eV/atom above the hull, so this region is likely a phase mixture.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (Ehull 0), so a single-phase film is plausible near Sb=0.667 (index 19). The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.37 eV is probably underestimated for a correlated Co2+ oxide, so I'm treating it as uninformative rather than against. Stable ternary phases are the best first probe.

Mild support. MACE puts spinel Co7Sb2O12 only 0.03 eV/atom above the hull, so it should form near Sb=0.22 (index 4). The earlier MEGNet gap of 1.44 eV for this phase is below 2.4 eV, so it should absorb. Index 19 (trirutile) gave about zero EQE, so the Co-rich side is the logical contrast.

Mostly uninformative. MACE puts CoSbO4 0.12 eV/atom above the hull, so films in the mid-range should be mixtures of spinel and trirutile rather than a new phase. The MEGNet gaps for Co spinels (0.8 eV) look unreliable. I'm measuring index 8, the GP-UCB pick in the unsampled gap between the two measured points, which are both near zero.
